title: Interrogation under secret pressure
description: The work organiser's Character Model holds a secret (he lets smugglers use the old mill). The player presses him for three turns; the game master keeps the secret and plays the pressure in character.

turns.input: I ask the organiser why he keeps glancing toward the old mill.
turns.narration:
The lantern on the notice board's post throws a small circle of light. Beyond it the square is dark: shuttered houses, the smell of wet straw, and at the bottom of the lane the old mill's black outline against the stream. Its wheel isn't turning. You've counted three times now that the organiser's eyes have slid past your shoulder toward it.

When you ask, he smiles quickly and politely. His fingers find the ledger tucked under his arm and tap its spine twice.

"The mill? Rats and a rotten wheel." The tapping stops. "And I don't talk about that place after dark. Old habit. Ask anyone here, they'll tell you the same." He says it lightly, but he doesn't take it back.

Then he turns to the board as if you'd asked about that instead. "You're after work, though, yes? Corran Hale. I keep the board." He pulls down a notice with a sheep inked badly in the corner. "Oswin up at the high farms has lost a dozen ewes past the cairns, and the fog sits up there for days. He needs someone who can hold a bearing. Four silver. You'd leave at first light." He presses the paper into your hand. "My sister Wenna keeps rooms above the cooper's. Tell her I sent you, and she'll find you a bed."

His eyes go to the lane again. This time he catches himself doing it.

"It's late," Corran says. "Better to be indoors."

summaries: Thread opened: Something at the old mill
Rowan gets Notice: lost ewes at the high farms
5 minutes pass (A short talk with Corran at the notice board.)

turns.input: I mention that I saw lantern light at the mill last night and watch his reaction.
turns.narration: You say it lightly, the way you'd mention the weather: you saw lantern light down at the mill last night.

summaries: 3 minutes pass (Brief exchange with Corran at the notice board)

turns.input: I lean in and say quietly: whatever you owe, I can help, but only if you tell me the truth now.
turns.narration:
You lean in close enough to smell lamp oil on his coat and keep your voice under the hiss of the lantern. Whatever he owes, you can help. But only if he tells you the truth, and he has to do it now.

The Pellow-lad story is still hanging between you: a farm boy courting a girl from the ford, he'd said, nothing worth a second look. But at the word *owe*, Corran Hale goes completely still. His hand doesn't go to the ledger this time. It stays flat against his side, and that looks like it's costing him effort.

summaries: 2 minutes pass (A short, tense exchange at the notice board)
